name: Running penalty (prefix count)
whenToUse: The standard answer: two passes, no extra array. Moving the closing hour by one changes the penalty by exactly 1.

card.signals: the penalty for a split point j counts things before j ('N') and after j ('Y'): a prefix count plus a suffix count, for every j from 0 to n.
card.pattern: a running prefix count. The first pass finds the penalty for j = 0 (the number of 'Y'). Then j moves right one hour at a time and the penalty changes by ±1. O(n) time.
card.coreIdea: Closing at j + 1 instead of j makes hour j open. If customers[j] = 'Y', those customers are no longer missed: penalty − 1. If it is 'N', the shop is now open for nobody: penalty + 1. Keep the lowest penalty and the first hour that reached it.
card.variant: prefix count kept in one variable. penalty(j) = ('N' in [0, j)) + ('Y' in [j, n)). Two prefix-count arrays of length n + 1 would give the same numbers, but each step only needs the previous penalty, so one variable is enough.

invariant: After hour j is processed, penalty = the penalty for closing at hour j + 1; best and best_hour are the lowest penalty and its earliest hour among 0..j + 1.

legend.text: j: the hour that becomes open
+1: an hour that adds to the penalty
open hours for the current closing hour
